newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian nickel, lead lose ground, others steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian nickel, lead lose ground, others steady.

text.p: Tin and nickel prices extended losses on the metal market on Friday, dealers said.

Lead lost ground while other base metals held steady in a narrow trading range. Lead prices fell by 100 rupees to 4,700 rupees per quintal on increased selling pressure following reports of a price cut of 3,000 rupees per tonne announced by state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd.

Tin fell further by 200 rupees to 35,100 rupees per quintal on higher arrivals of the imported metal. Tin was down by 200 rupees per quintal on Thursday. Nickel moved down by 200 rupees to 37,300 rupees per quintal on the back of weak world trends.
Copper was steady at 11,650 rupees per quintal, as was zinc at 6,250 rupees per quintal in limited activity.

"State-owned Hindustan Copper and Hindustan Zinc Ltd. left prices of copper and zinc for November unchanged but they have now started offering discounts if buyers pay cash immediately," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
